subject: Error While Attempting to Convert Data to Telemetry

messages.author: 0cb1ab1dff2bfeb6
messages.subject: Error While Attempting to Convert Data to Telemetry
parts:
Hello, 
I've been attempting to clean up and manipulate some gila monster data so I can convert it into a telemetry object for AKDE calculations. I've managed to clean up the date, time, add a UTM zone, and even a timestamp consisting of the combined date and time. When I try to convert the data to a telemetry object I get the following error:

gila.tonto.clean<-as.telemetry(gila.tonto.clean, timeformat="auto",timezone="UTC", projection=UTM,datum=NAD27, timeout=Inf,
                     na.rm="row",mark.rm=FALSE,keep=FALSE,drop=TRUE)

Error in rgdal::project(XY[i, , drop = FALSE], zone[i], inv = TRUE) : target crs creation failed: Invalid value for an argument.

I'm not sure what's causing the error or how to solve it. Any insight would be appreciated. Thanks! 

Jason

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Error While Attempting to Convert Data to Telemetry
parts:
Hi Jason,

I'm guessing that UTM and NAD27 are undefined variables in R? Those arguments need to be PROJ4 formatted or omitted. Does it work if you leave them out?

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Re: Error While Attempting to Convert Data to Telemetry
parts:
Hi Jason,

Chris has made ctmm really flexible in automatically detecting coordinate information, but he can’t perfectly predict how folks will label their data, and there are a near-infinite number of ways this can be done.

Specify the projection in a PROJ4 string like this: 

“ +proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=NAD27 +units=m +no_defs”

Alternatively, you can just reproject into latlong.

Jesse

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Re: Error While Attempting to Convert Data to Telemetry
parts:
Hi Jason,

Strangely, the rgdal (and successor sf)  package don't seem to accept the latitude band any more, even though I'm almost certain they did in the past.
If you cutoff the band to UTM.zone="12", then the data imports without errors, and the points are in Arizona. However, since your datum is both not all the default WGS84 and not all consistent across the rows, you want to include that in the UTM.zone column, like

UTM.zone
"12 +datum=WGS84"
"12 +datum=WGS84"
"12 +datum=WGS84"
"12 +datum=NAD27"
"12 +datum=NAD27"
"12 +datum=NAD27"

and delete the rows with missing data, because they have no valid zone and will also throw an error.

Best,
Chris
